content.text:
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
MT will see strong year-over-year margin expansion, and MT should improve sequentially in Q2. We expect that CCT margin will be approximately flat year-over-year, given the anticipated revenue decline. As a result, adjusted EPS will grow roughly 20% in Q2, and essentially be in line with Q1. Our tax rate remains at 21%, and interest expense will remain at an elevated level. Let me now turn the call back to Luca on slide nine.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Emmanuel. Before we move to the best part of the call, the Q&A, just a few points. This quarter, we focused on growth and execution in everything we did, and we delivered a strong performance. Through increased orders, project awards, and large green energy wins, we delivered on growth. Through our cash performance, capital deployment, and operational improvements, we delivered on execution.
The awards and share gains we're bringing home and our execution, give us the confidence to deliver on our long-term targets: 6% top-line growth, 20% segment margin, 10%+ EPS growth, and 12% free cash flow margin. We are proud of our performance this quarter and never satisfied, so our journey continues. I would like to thank all our stakeholders for their continued support of ITT. It has been my pleasure speaking with you all this morning. Elliot, please open the line for questions.
Operator
Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. At this time, if you have a question or comment, please press star one on your touchtone phone. If at any point your question has been answered, you may remove yourself from the queue by pressing the pound key. Again, we do ask that while you pose your question, you pick up your handset to provide optimal sound quality. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Thank you. Our first question today comes from Jeff Hammond from KeyBanc Capital Markets. Your line is open.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
Hey, good morning, gentlemen.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Hi, Jeff.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
Just to start within your unchanged organic growth guidance, there seems to be some moving pieces around, IP coming in better, some of this friction destock and softness in CCT. Can you just maybe speak to how you're thinking about the segments differently from an organic growth standpoint for the year?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
I think you got it, Jeff. I think that IP is, has come out stronger in Q1, and we see the strength in projects and also the strength in the short cycle in Q1. So, probably IP will be better for the year. We continue to see the outperformance in the OE friction, but, I will say the aftermarket in Motion Technologies in automotive is probably be, slower than what we expected. The destocking will last for the entire year. And then when it comes to the connector side of the business, also the destocking of the connectors will probably last for the full year of 2023. This is really how it plays.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
Okay. And then just on the destock, what usually these are sharper destocks, and then you're settled. What makes you think that these destocks carry through the year?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
When it comes to the automotive, really talking to our customers and really the feedback that we're getting from them. When you look at the distribution on the, on the connectors, for example, we see the decline in the, in the orders, but see, we still see the, inventory level still high. So when we look at the point of sales, their bookings and the inventory level, we do our simulation, we talk to our distributors, and, we think that this is going to last a little bit longer. This is how we got that.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
On CCT?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
That was on CCT.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
Okay.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
That I was talking about the distributors on the, on the connector side, Jeff.
Jeff Hammond
Managing Director, KeyCorp
Okay. Okay. Okay, great. I'll get back in queue. Thanks.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Jeff.
Operator
Our next question comes from Scott Davis, from Melius Research. Your line is open.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Morning, Scott.
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
Hi. Good morning, guys.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Morning, Scott.
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
Good morning. Presentation is really pretty clear, so I wanted to take a step back a little bit and talk a little bit about this anti-flaring technology. What, what is it that you guys are doing different? And, and maybe just help us understand what that really means. I would imagine there's a lot of those types of projects out there, if your technology-
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
... is perhaps differentiated or interesting or whatever, but I'll, I'll let you guys address that. Thank you.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Yeah. Let me give you a couple of examples because the decarbonization is the anti-flaring, stop the flaring, but it's also the carbon capture. So when you have the flaring, for example, also normal wells in the Permian Basin, you extract the oil, and it comes out oil, water, and gas. And usually what happens, you separate there and then, and you separate oil from water, and you flare the gas.
Now, with our Bornemann pumps, which are multi-phase boosting technology, practically are twin screw pumps, where you pump, you can pump water, gas, and liquid together in all the different mixes. What you take, you take all that mix, you pump it 50, 60km down the line so that you separate where you can actually use the gas and put the gas in distribution.
That is, the twin screw pumps, that is the multi-phase pump, that will stop the flaring. The decarbonization is something similar in the sense that, what we do, for instance, in this major site in Australia, what you have, you have the offshore field that produce gas containing CO2. The CO2 is then separated by the gas, at the gas plant, and then our pumps will take that CO2, mix with water and push it down 2km below the ground. And that is for the carbon capture.
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
Oh, pretty cool. I actually didn't know you could pump both a liquid and a gas at the same time, so thanks for that. The Continental deal, why do you need those, why do you need them? I guess is the question. Is it a question of-
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
... channel access and brand, do you cannibalize yourself a little bit because you're both then going to market, but under different brands? Perhaps just help me understand how the dynamics of that, how that works. Thanks.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yeah. Yeah, yeah, Scott. The partnership with Continental is really crucial for our friction business. As at friction we're we excel at producing high quality parts, and that we deliver on time. And we have great also material science. What we don't know how to do is distribute and market our products in the aftermarket.
And this is why Continental is so key for us, because they deliver that aspect of distribution, marketing, and branding, and we focus on what we know how to do. And so it's really the perfect combination between and playing to our strength, to our respective strengths with this agreement. So a really key strategic partnership. We have a 10-year partnership that we renewed, and we look for much more in the future.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
And also, Scott, think about it, if you go with Continental, the distributor, you have thousands of products you can offer them, where we are going there only with the brake pads, so they have a good value proposition.
Scott Davis
Founding Partner, Chairman, and CEO, Melius Research
That sounds interesting. Thank you, guys. Best of luck. Congrats on the start of the year.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Scott.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Thanks.
Operator
Our next question comes from Vlad Bystricky from Citigroup. Your line is open.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Morning, Vlad.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Hi, Vlad.
Vlad Bystricky
Vice President and Equity Research Analyst, Citigroup
Morning, guys. Thanks for taking my call. So can you just talk about on the IP business, your level of confidence or visibility in the baseline pumps business continuing to perform well here, and what you're hearing from your distributors about inventory in the channel there, and any concerns about potential destocking to emerge in that business?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yeah, sure. So, I have to say that in Q1, we were a little bit surprised positively by the order rate of our baseline business. The baseline business was up, even though it was more driven by price than volume. Volume was actually a little bit down, but much better than what we were expecting. And when we checked with our distributors, they don't report any excess inventory situation.
So I would say that for the moment, it looks like our differentiation, which is providing reliable pumps that our customers know and that are easily swappable in good lead times compared to the competition, is really what's differentiating for our distributors and their customers. So pretty good start of the year for baseline.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
And one other point as well to add to what Emmanuel said, is that if you look at our short cycle orders were also up sequentially, Q1 over Q4, which is a positive sign.
Vlad Bystricky
Vice President and Equity Research Analyst, Citigroup
Okay. That's, that's all really helpful color. And then maybe just shifting to Motion Tech. You highlighted again the OE wins in the quarter out share, to drive share gains over time. Can you just talk about in China specifically, your-
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure
Vlad Bystricky
Vice President and Equity Research Analyst, Citigroup
... wins and share with China OEMs versus foreign OEMs?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Yeah. I'm glad that you asked this question because I was in China in Q1. And everybody is reading on the newspaper that the Chinese OEMs are gaining shares. But you don't really smell, you don't touch them until you get there, and you drive from Pudong to Puxi, and actually, I can tell you, Vlad, I couldn't recognize any of the cars on the highway.
They were completely different from when I was there three years ago. All these new OEMs, that many of them were electric. So you really touch the importance of the Chinese OEMs. When you look at our data, in 2022, 62% of the brake pads that we produced in 2022, were for the Chinese OEMs.
The market share of the Chinese OEM in the China market is above 50. So we are very well positioned with them, with many of them. If it's NIO, if it's XPENG, if it's Li Auto or if it is BYD, all, all of them. So I want to give credit to the China team, because when we went to China eight, nine, 10 years ago, we went with one customer, one Western customer. We reduced the risk, we differentiated with all the Western, and several years ago, the team decided to go Chinese, and this is paying off.
Vlad Bystricky
Vice President and Equity Research Analyst, Citigroup
Now, that's great to hear, Luca. I'll get back into the few things.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Matt.
Operator
Our next question comes from Mike Halloran with Baird. Your line is open.
Mark Macaluso
Vice President of Investor Relations and Head of Global Communications, ITT
Morning, Mike.
Mike Halloran
Senior Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Hey, good morning, everyone.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Morning, Mike. Morning.
Mike Halloran
Senior Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Let's stick on the auto side. Certainly appreciate the destock that's happening, but Luca, as I said last quarter, I think you always give really good context on how you think the auto market holistically is going to perform. If you could give some thoughts by region on what you're seeing, that'd be great.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure. So, I would say Q1, really, the market performed in the way the IHS forecasted. So when you look at the market, you have Europe that performed very well, +17% in the quarter. China was down 8%, and North America was up almost 10%. Now, we outperformed the market, roughly in Q1, by more than 100 basis points overall.
Now, the way that the forecast is from IHS is still around 85.5 million vehicles. They are forecasting mid-single digit growth for Europe and North America, flatish China. What our assumptions are, Mike, is the market will probably grow low single digit worldwide, North America, positive, mid-single digits, Europe and China, flatish. Now, with those assumptions we are always more conservative. We expect always to outgrow the market by roughly 400 to 500 basis points. The reason why we tend to be a little bit more conservative is also because we start seeing the level of inventory going up a little bit.
Mike Halloran
Senior Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Mm. No, that makes sense. Backlog, obviously, still really strong. Maybe talk about how you're expecting that to normalize as you work through the year and how that's embedded in the guide.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Sure. Yeah,
Mike Halloran
Senior Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird
That's a holistic question, by the way, not just tied to, not just tied to motion.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
No, no, no, for sure. One thing that when we entered Q1, we weren't thinking that we were able to grow backlog even further when, where that the record we had, and in fact, we did. We grew backlog even by another $70 million this quarter. And if you look at our two main businesses, where backlog is really a key metric, IP backlog grew sequentially 10% versus prior; we're up 30%.
And then in terms of CCT, our backlog grew 13% versus prior year, pretty stable sequentially. But both businesses add book to bill above, largely above 1.0. So really good news from a backlog standpoint. As Luca mentioned, especially in IP, where you have a lot of projects, a growing presence of our projects in the backlog, that backlog is also getting more and more profitable.
Mike Halloran
Senior Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Great. Really appreciate it. Thank you.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Mike.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Thanks, Mike.
Operator
Our next question comes from Damian Karas with UBS. Your line is open.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Hi.
Mark Macaluso
Vice President of Investor Relations and Head of Global Communications, ITT
Morning, Damian.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Morning, everyone.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Hi, Damian.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Morning. I wanted to ask you guys, first on IP margin, the performance remains quite impressive, especially when you compare that to what we see from some of the other pump and valve manufacturers out there. So, Luca, I'd like to hear your thoughts on how sustainable this profitability is. Have you gotten any customer pushback on some of the pricing actions? And how are you thinking about any potential market share impacts as a result?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure. Let me address the pricing action first. We are pricing when we win a project, we are very diligent. This is the first things. But we are pricing in market, so what you are finding is that the cost competitiveness of IP is really top-notch, and we are managing this project very well in terms of from an execution point of view, changes, et cetera, which obviously improve the profitability of the business. So, I would say no pushback at all when it comes to pricing. And the approach that we're having today is really value-based, the value that we are delivering to the customer, the value that we are delivering to the company.
And this is what many of the customers are willing to pay. So that's on the first point. When it comes to sustainability, listen, this is the third quarter in a row. Obviously, the business is performing well. The sites are performing well. There are opportunities to continue to improve, but there is also a lot of investments that we need to make in this business. The relayout of Seneca Falls more VAV, more investment on the product side, so in systems. So, those investment will need to be paid for, and this is something we need to bear in mind.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Understood. Thank you. And I have a follow-up question on the Continental agreement. You mentioned partnering with them in China. Could you maybe tell us a little bit more about that? I mean, what's the aftermarket opportunity there? I'm assuming it's a pretty competitive market, so what angle-
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Are you thinking about playing there?
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure, Damian. Actually, what, what we are saying is that, China really gives us the flexibility, and, with China is not with Continental. So the agreement with Continental is mainly a European agreement for the European market. And in Continental, we have the flexibility to, to go ourselves and to try different things. Also, because it's a very different market, very entrepreneurial, and we, we need to test different things over there.
Damian Karas
Senior Equity Research Analyst of Industrials / Tech, UBS
Understood. Understood. Thank you very much. Appreciate it.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thank you, Damian.
Operator
Our next question comes from Nathan Jones with Stifel. Your line is open.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Good morning, this is Matt on for Nathan Jones.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Hi.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Morning.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Hi, morning. So you guys mentioned a lot about short cycle pump orders. I just wanted to ask, see if you could talk about the funnel of longer cycle project opportunities and your expectations for potential orders in 2023.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Sure. So, when you look at the funnel today, we have an ever-growing funnel. The total funnel we're seeing is around $1 billion for IP. And half is basically oil and gas or energy, and half is the rest of the industry, so chemical, mining, and other stuff. And then really it's growing pretty much everywhere. Obviously, North America is growing the fastest, but Europe is going back to a growth path. And it's even increasing, so that's year-over-year, and on a sequential basis, it's still increasing by high single digits.
In terms of industry, that's what we see, the largest increase are around oil and gas, chemical, and mining, but even general industrial is participating into that growth. So we're seeing a very dynamic funnel. Despite all the orders that we've been acquiring, the funnel keeps on growing. So for us, it's a really good sign.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
It's good to hear. And then, could you talk about the price cost dynamics and the different pieces of business?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Sure. So let me start by saying that, from a price cost standpoint, this quarter we were neutral, from a dollar standpoint. We were seeing is that continued good performance from a pricing cost standpoint in IP, that more than covers our total inflation. In MT, the situation is still very difficult, especially in friction, where we don't get 100% of our cost inflation covered, but that's, but we're progressing . That's, it's a matter of progressing small percentage points over what we did last year. Then, in CCT, we're really starting with the value-based pricing.
So we're seeing aSure. So let me start by saying that, from a price cost standpoint, this quarter we were neutral, from a dollar standpoint. What we're seeing is that continued good performance from a pricing standpoint in IP, that more than covers our total inflation. In MT, the situation is still very difficult, especially in friction, where we don't get 100% of our cost inflation covered, but that's, but we're progressing. That's, it's a matter of progressing small percentage points over what we did last year. Then in CCT, we're really starting with the value-based pricing. price cost equation that is that's little bit tilted towards the negative, but we expect this to really change in the next few quarter as we're able to execute on our value-based pricing plan.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Got it. Thank you.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks.
Operator
Our next question comes from Joe Ritchie with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Morning, Joe.
Joe Ritchie
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Thanks. Good morning, guys.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Hi, Joe.
Joe Ritchie
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Hey, so, I wanted to start in with Industrial Process margins. Greater than 21% now, three quarters in a row. I know we've asked a few questions about this already. The two questions I have are, number one, is this the right baseline moving forward? And number two, like, your projects business was up over 50% this quarter. Typically, I think we would think about it as being mixed negative, but clearly, it's not having an impact on your business. So maybe just talk through some of the dynamics about how you're managing your project margins, and why you're still getting that leverage on them.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
So let me start, and Emmanuel, please jump in. So, yes, the project business, the order of projects are up 54%. And by the way, the compare was not an easy one because the growth Q1 last year was 45%, so it's really good in terms of value. Now, the profitability of these projects is the highest it's ever been.
The profitability of the projects backlog that we have is the highest it has ever been. Not comparable to the short cycle, of course, but we have never seen that level of profitability. And this is the result of a very rigorous process in the order acquisition. The sales are very disciplined and also a very good execution.
If you think about Saudi Arabia delivering 100% on-time delivery, this means that, your negotiation with the customer are going very well. You can, you can ask the changes, you have a customer experience, very positive, which also facilitate any negotiation that you have on price and on changes.
Now, this quarter, we had actually a headwind, even if it was a small one, in terms of mix, roughly 20 basis points headwind. We will see this headwind probably become a little bit bigger in the future, Joe, because today, the backlog that we do have is 48% projects, 52% short cycle. You remember last year was 60/40, 60 short cycle, 40 projects, and I do expect by the end of the year to be 60/40, with 60 being projects. So that will probably be a headwind, but not a one that we cannot manage.
Joe Ritchie
Managing Director, Goldman Sachs
Got it. And just to follow up, that was helpful, Luca, but so to 21%, probably not the right jumping off point, but in and around that area going forward and with mix potentially being an impact, is that the right way to think about it?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yeah, yeah, yeah, Joe, that's the right way to think about it. We are for sure we're not going back to 15%, so we're in that vicinity the 19% to 20%. And there's a lot more work that is needed, as Luca said, in terms of investment, to make sure that we continuously improve. And also in IP, there's a lot more opportunities that we need to go after. We still have a couple sites that are losing money in IP that we want to go after.
So, I think that's the IP situation from a margin standpoint has been really, really positive for us, and very much faster than what we were anticipated from a margin expansion standpoint.
Bryan Blair
Managing Director & Senior Analyst, Industrial Machinery and Flow Control, Oppenheimer
Okay, great. I'll leave it there. Thanks, guys.
Mark Macaluso
Vice President of Investor Relations and Head of Global Communications, ITT
Thanks, Joe.
Operator
Our next question comes from Matt Summerville, from D.A. Davidson. Your line is open.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Morning, Matt.
Matt Summerville
Managing Director & Senior Research Analyst, Industrial Technology, D.A. Davidson
Thanks. Just a couple quick-- morning. Just, a couple quick questions. Just on, on MT, what does the pathway look like to get back to where margins were in either 2020, 2021, more firmly into the high teens? Is it a matter of closing that gap between price cost? Is it a matter of, of mixed normalization? Can you talk about timing and, and walk through how we should be thinking about the margin progression in that business?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yep. So, let's say around 2019-2020, MT was around 18% margin. So if being at a little less than 15% right now, we still have quite a bit to go. But I would say we're pretty confident in us being able to get to that level of margin of around 18% in 2024. I would say a couple of things to think about. The first one is, obviously, we're driving pricing as much as we can to cover our costs. We have a slew of new platforms that are going to enter into production in the next few years, that have been priced with a level of raw material pricing that is the one that we're seeing today.
So we don't expect to be impacted as much by the price cost equation. Then productivity is central to MT, and this is something that has been difficult during the pandemic and the supply chain disruptions. We are firmly back on track, and so I expect that Motion Tech productivity will contribute to the Motion Tech margin expansion.
Matt Summerville
Managing Director & Senior Research Analyst, Industrial Technology, D.A. Davidson
Well, just as a quick follow-up, with respect to IP, obviously pretty, pretty strong margin performance for a handful of quarters now. How much of that is being driven by the lean initiatives out of Seneca Falls, and is there still incremental margin benefit to be realized? And if so, is there a way to quantify that?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yeah. So, I would say that lean in Seneca Falls and outside of Seneca Falls has been contributing quite a bit between 150 to 200 basis points. And obviously, what's best about it is that we're nowhere near to be done. So, a lot more potential there. I would say also price has been a really large contributor, as we mentioned, right? This quarter price had a positive impact of over 500 basis points in terms of, from a margin standpoint. Which allows us to offset, obviously, the cost inflation and the negative mix that Luca was talking about.
So, a lot more in the tank for IP to continuously expand from a margin standpoint.
Matt Summerville
Managing Director & Senior Research Analyst, Industrial Technology, D.A. Davidson
Understood. Thanks, guys.
Mark Macaluso
Vice President of Investor Relations and Head of Global Communications, ITT
Thanks, Matt. Thanks.
Operator
Our next question comes from Brian Blair with Oppenheimer. Your line is open.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Morning, Brian.
Mark Macaluso
Vice President of Investor Relations and Head of Global Communications, ITT
Morning, Brian.
Bryan Blair
Managing Director & Senior Analyst, Industrial Machinery and Flow Control, Oppenheimer
Thank you. Good morning, guys. Wanted to quickly circle back on the flexibility that the Continental Agreement affords you to go on your own in China in the aftermarket. We really haven't focused on that opportunity quite as much, and I think it's still a relatively small scale for you guys. I recall, going back a while, but pre-pandemic, maybe it was $10 million, a little over $10 million in revenue at that point. Can you speak to the current run rate revenue in China aftermarket, and what the future may hold there potential size of that revenue stream looking forward?
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Sure. So, our aftermarket business in China is a little less than $5 million dollars in terms of revenue for the year. So it's quite a bit smaller than what we are in Europe, but it's also understandable because we are a relatively new player in China. We've been there for 10 years. So we don't have the product portfolio than the that maybe people that have been there for longer have. And then also we don't have the distribution as we do have it in Europe. So I think that the great thing about the agreement is that it frees us up to really go the way we want in China.
So we have been talking to several partners to see if they would like to do the distribution and the marketing for us. This is still something that is evolving. We're trying to really build the business case for the China business aftermarket. But I think that for us, this... The important thing was to have the option and to be able to work on a, on, on a business model that really going to play to our strength.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Okay, definitely makes sense. And perhaps offer a little more background on Micro-Mode, the unique technology that they offer and trailing or expected growth rates. And please confirm deal valuation. Look, I believe you said around 11 times EBITDA, that implies a rather attractive margin profile.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Yeah. So, yeah, is 11x EBITDA. That's correct, Brian. Now, what we like about Micro-Mode is that their focus on space and defense is in the market where we play, where we're strong. They have a complementary set of products to the one that we have. We do not have the highly customized radio frequency and hermetic connectors for harsh application that they can offer.
And, when Emmanuel and I visited the site in California, we were also very pleased to see the investment that they made from a manufacturing point of view. The site that they have there is a very simple, and, but nice vertically integrated. So that will fit very well with the way that we want to expand.
The team there have got very good expertise on product and process as well. So very, very synergistic, and I can tell you, yesterday was the first day. I was talking to the team last night, and they're already working on a couple of opportunities together that will allow MicroMode to grow. So, very, very good acquisition for the connector business, a platform that we want to grow organically and inorganically.
Matt DeYoe
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Very helpful color. Thank you.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thank you.
Operator
Our last question comes from Michael Anastasiou with TD Cowen. Your line is open.
Michael Anastasiou
Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Morning.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Morning.
Michael Anastasiou
Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Hey, good morning, guys. Thanks for taking my question. So CCT saw year-over-year increases, but it seems like order growth was offset from weakness, maybe on the industrial side. Can you just provide some color there, on order cadence throughout the quarter on specifically the industrial side? Any end market commentary there would be helpful. Thank you.
Emmanuel Caprais
SVP & CFO, ITT
Yeah, Michael, so you're right. The industrial side of our connector business is the one that has declined and has really offset all the good growth we're seeing in aero, in aero and defense. So our industrial connector business in the quarter from an order standpoint declined by 21%, which caused our connector business to decline by 17%, 17%. And this is driven by industrial and also what's in the periphery of industrial, such as medical, for instance. So I think that we're monitoring that. Luca mentioned that the inventory at our distributors is, has not gone down.
So what we're seeing today is that they're reflecting the improvement in the supply chain, and so they don't need to pre-order as many components, but we don't see yet the inventory declining. We're seeing some of their POS data that is stabilizing, so that makes us a little bit hopeful. But we think that in terms from a, from an inventory reduction standpoint, they haven't really started reducing inventory. And the last point I wanted to make is that we checked on the market side, and it's really a market-driven event, and it's not really driven by our ability to supply connectors to them.
Michael Anastasiou
Research Analyst, TD Cowen
Great. Thank you. That's helpful.
Luca Savi
CEO and President, ITT
Thanks, Michael.
Operator
Thank you. This does conclude today's teleconference. Please disconnect your lines at this time and have a wonderful day.
